//: dashboard/dashboard.config.example.json -- copy to dashboard.config.json and edit.
//1: DOCS ONLY: the service never auto-loads a *.example.json file.
//2: Precedence PER KEY: CLI flag > RC_DASH_* env var > this file > built-in default.
//3: Omitted keys fall back to a built-in default that PROBES a candidate list.
//4: Run `uv run python -m rc_dashboard --print-config` to see what each key
//5: actually resolved to and why, and `--check-feeds` to see what is on disk.
//6: Every '//'-prefixed key is stripped by the loader, so comments are legal here.
//risk: What counts as risky differs by cluster: switch built-in rules off, change or add
//risk1: them, and set this cluster's variables. Usually kept in its own file and named by
//risk2: `profile` (or RC_DASH_RISK_PROFILE). Every key: risk-profiles/README.md and example.json.
//ask: Chat with LLM: each question runs an agent CLI on this host, as the service's
//ask1: user (the `codex` preset uses that user's Codex login), with a compact, masked
//ask2: snapshot of the window on screen. That snapshot leaves the host. Off by default, and
//ask3: refused while server.auth.password_hash is empty. The agent can read whatever the
//ask4: service's account can read: run the service as a dedicated account, not a person's.

ask.//command: or any CLI: argv list or one string; prompt on stdin, answer on stdout
ask.//env_passthrough: the agent gets only what a program needs of the service's environment;
ask.//env_passthrough1: name what else it needs here, as names or NAME_* prefixes (3+ characters before _*), for a provider
ask.//context_kb: each question's data budget: the whole window's (the Ask LLM tab), or one
ask.//context_kb1: panel's or one session's (a panel's ask button); all use the same agent
ask.//include_commands: masked command lines in that data; a session's outline names the
ask.//include_commands1: commands it ran either way, never their arguments unless this is on
ask.//system_prompt: the answerer's instructions; empty uses the built-in one. A file is
ask.//system_prompt1: re-read on every question and wins. {deployment} {site} {window} are filled in.
ask.//citations: every row the model is given carries a ref it cites after each figure; the
ask.//citations1: page links each to its row, with a preview of what the model saw. false: none

//annotate: The session inspector's 'annotate purposes': what each tool call was for, asked of a
//annotate1: model. OFF by default: it sends each call's command line (masked, as the page shows it)
//annotate2: and its folder to the provider. provider: anthropic | openai (any OpenAI-compatible
//annotate3: endpoint: set base_url for vLLM, Ollama, LiteLLM, ...) | codex | claude (the CLIs, with
//annotate4: this user's login) | ask (the chat's agent) | command (prompt on stdin, JSON on stdout or
//annotate5: in {answer_file}). model empty: the provider's default (anthropic: claude-opus-5-5;
//annotate6: openai has none). The key: the env var api_key_env names (empty: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or
//annotate7: OPENAI_API_KEY), else api_key_file, else api_key (never shown by /api/config). effort:
//annotate8: anthropic's output_config.effort, empty to leave it out. Answers are kept in
//annotate9: <cache.dir>/annotate/purposes.jsonl, so a command is asked about once per model.
//ui: What the page opens on before a reader changes it; ignored by the saved builds.
//ui0: node_noun: what the watched hosts are called, as in 'Login nodes right now'.
//ui1: user_columns: Active users' columns, any of agents ides running exited cpu read
//ui2: written sent received gpu last. A reader's own choice is kept in their browser.
//ui3: routine_commands: what a trajectory's tree hides when 'hide routine' is on, beside
//ui4: runs of the same command: a command, a command and its first argument, or
//ui5: 'shell-snapshot' (an agent's shell sourcing its saved environment). A shell that
//ui6: ran only these, or one of them piped through filters (ps | grep root), goes too.
//anonymize: Replace every username, lab or Slurm account name, email address and numeric
//anonymize1: user ID in what the service sends out with a stable alias (user-7f3a9c1e,
//anonymize2: lab-1b2c3d4e). Off by default. salt empty: one is generated into
//anonymize3: <cache.dir>/anonymize.salt and reused; changing it reshuffles every alias, and
//anonymize4: the page never shows it. Empty pattern lists use anonymize.py's defaults (homes
//anonymize5: and FAS lab trees); set them for a cluster laid out differently. Switching any
//anonymize6: of this costs a restart, never a rebuild. RC_DASH_ANONYMIZE=1 turns it on.

feeds.//1a: already ends in /logs. Both files are globbed; each record carries its own host.
feeds.//2: List every root to merge; a non-existent root is reported, never fatal.

ebpf.//x: days must COVER live.retention_min, or the far end of the widest
ebpf.//y: window reads as a gap: 8 = 7 days of retention + one, because hosts
ebpf.//z: roll over independently and the oldest day is still being written.
ebpf.//3: max_age_s: residency_totals is written UNCONDITIONALLY every
ebpf.//4: EBPFM_RESIDENCY_S (default 60s) whether or not anything was tracked,
ebpf.//5: so freshness here means liveness, not activity. 300 = 5 ticks, the same

feeds.//7: Node tier (unprivileged): node_snapshot.py is a vendored copy of
feeds.//8: collect/common/snapshot.py, so log/login is schema-compatible and works
feeds.//9: as a stand-in before `ebpfm --node` is deployed anywhere.

ebpf_node.//10: 2 snapshots: per_user_cgroup.cpu_usage_usec is CUMULATIVE, so a per-user
ebpf_node.//11: CPU rate only exists as a delta between two consecutive snapshots.

feeds.//12: collect/slurm_query.bash writes ONE FILE PER DAY into DEST_DIR, named
feeds.//13: SlurmData_<start>_<stop>-orig.csv. Point `dir` at DEST_DIR, not at a file.
feeds.//14: NOTE: sacct -D --starttime/--endtime overlap at midnight, so a job spanning
feeds.//15: two days appears in BOTH day-files; the reducer dedups on JobID.

//16: RETENTION vs WINDOW. retention_min is what the process HOLDS and the
//17: ceiling the page's picker can reach; window_min is only the view a fresh
//18: page opens on. Any window up to retention is an exact slice of the same
//19: per-minute BUCKETS -- never buffered raw events, which are ~10-20 GB/day
//20: fleet-wide. Raising window_min is free; raising retention_min costs
//21: memory (one slot per minute) and a longer startup backfill.

live.//22: Offered in the picker. Anything above retention_min is DROPPED from
live.//23: the list rather than offered and then silently clamped.
live.//24: backfill_hours: how far back the startup read reaches, capped at
live.//25: retention. It runs on EVERY start, newest first, from the collector's
live.//26: files -- nothing this service wrote is ever restored -- so what the
live.//27: page holds never depends on whether the service was up while the data
live.//28: was collected. 0 starts empty and fills forward. Progress is on
live.//29: /api/feeds, and /api/live reports `retained_from`, so a short feed
live.//29a: reads as a gap in the oldest bins instead of as a quiet fleet.

//30: The historical reducers (quantiles, CCDFs, Gini, the dedup index) hold
//31: no time index and are not resumable from a byte offset, so a window
//32: change REBUILDS them from the rows -- seeking past everything older, so
//33: the cost is the window and not the day.

panels.//34: How many built windows to keep. Each costs reducer state, not just a
panels.//35: payload; 2 lets a reader compare a narrow and a wide view.
panels.//36: A built window keeps ingesting, so it drifts past its own span. It
panels.//37: re-scans once drift reaches this share of the window -- proportional,
panels.//38: so 1h refreshes often and cheaply and 7d rarely and expensively. The
panels.//39: drift is published either way; it is never rounded away.
panels.//40: Every built window is saved to <cache.dir>/windows with how far into
panels.//41: each day-file it read, so a restart -- run.sh restarts on every save --
panels.//42: or a return to an evicted window reads only what was written since,
panels.//43: not the whole window. Used only by the same code and config, only while
panels.//44: the files it read are unchanged, and only while younger than the drift
panels.//45: budget above. ~12 MB per day of window per login node; keep bounds it.
panels.//h1: Reduce each record once, into the state of its epoch hour, saved under
panels.//h2: <cache.dir>/hours; a window is its first part-hour read as before, its
panels.//h3: whole hours merged from their saved states, and the open hour read as
panels.//h4: before. A window switch, a drift refresh or a restart then costs those
panels.//h5: edges and a merge, not a re-read. Filtered views are still read.
panels.//h6: An hour closes once the newest record is this far past its end; a
panels.//h7: record later still is merged into its hour's saved state, not lost.
panels.//h8: Also save each whole epoch day as one merged state (7 d = ~7 merges).
panels.//h9: Pause between two hours' reductions, so a backlog never holds off the live tier.

//history: Every sealed (.jsonl.gz) day-file of the eBPF tier kept as Parquet under `dir`
//history1: (empty: <cache.dir>/history), converted in the background in `workers` processes
//history2: (0: up to 8, as the CPUs allow). A selective read of a sealed file, and a search of
//history3: it by time, is answered from its copy once there is one; nothing waits for it.
//history4: `days`: the newest dated dirs kept, 0 for every one the source holds.
//history5: enabled: false (RC_DASH_HISTORY=0) reads every day-file as JSONL. Switching it,
//history6: or moving `dir`, rebuilds no saved window or hour: a copy reads as its file does.

trajectories.//2: idle_evict_s never reaches INSIDE the selected window -- the real
trajectories.//3: cutoff is max(idle_evict_s, window). Otherwise the panel would rank
trajectories.//4: 'sessions active in the last 2h' while labelling itself 24h.
trajectories.//5: max_sessions is therefore the memory bound, and it applies PER held
trajectories.//6: window: lower it if you raise live.retention_min on a busy fleet.
trajectories.//7: Past it, whole sessions (process trees) go, the least recently active
trajectories.//8: first. A FAS login node makes 45k keys on a median day, 105k at most,
trajectories.//9: and each held costs about 6 KB: 150k holds a busy day whole.
trajectories.//10: The session inspector's read builds a session's records in inspect_workers
trajectories.//11: worker processes (no more than the CPUs it may use); 1 builds them in the
trajectories.//12: service's own process. The same records either way (keysearch.py).
trajectories.//: 'usr' is excluded: a usr-keyed group is 'everything that user did',
trajectories.//1: which is not a trajectory. It is counted in by_key_type, never ranked.

//server: auth.password_hash: a salted scrypt hash of the one password readers sign in with.
//server1: `python -m rc_dashboard new-password` makes the password, writes it to a file only you
//server2: can read, and prints the hash. Empty: `serve` refuses to start, unless auth.open (--open,
//server3: RC_DASH_OPEN=1) serves the page with no sign-in to anyone who reaches the port. A session
//server3a: lasts auth.session_days. A new password signs everyone out.
//server4: rdns: name the Network bytes panel's endpoints by reverse DNS from this host, `workers`
//server5: lookups at a time, off the request path, kept in <cache.dir>/rdns.json. Off: names come
//server6: only from the records' command lines. A restart, never a rebuild.
//server7: gil_switch_ms: how long one thread may hold the GIL while another waits for it
//server8: (Python's own: 5 ms). A build and the backfill keep it; the event loop gives it up at
//server9: every read and write. 1 keeps the page answering beside a build. 0 keeps Python's.
//server10: allowed_origins: a websocket opened by a page on any other origin (another port too) is refused; list the
//server11: origins of a proxy that rewrites the Host ("https://dash.example.org"). allowed_hosts:
//server12: with no password, a request is answered only under a loopback name, `host`, or one of
//server13: these ("*": any), against DNS rebinding. Unused with a password. dev_origins: a dev
//server14: server's origins, added to allowed_origins; run.sh sets them (RC_DASH_DEV_ORIGINS) in dev mode.
